cases.name: principal_control_realm_id_is_event_derived_and_nonzero_nibble_rejected
cases.note: Step 1 of the human PCR genesis unit. Every value below is recomputed from the canonical preimage bytes: the identity bindings are read out of the hashed bytes rather than declared beside them, and the rejected Realm token is derived from the accepted one by changing only the reserved high nibble.

founding_material.note: The genesis payload embeds this exact descriptor and the second Event carries this exact authorize payload, so the two fixtures are one construction input and not two copies that can drift apart.

accepted_form.note: Realm ids are event-derived: the Realm token equals its ak.realm.create Event token byte for byte and retyping only swaps the typed prefix.

rejected_form.derived_from: the accepted realm_id, changing only the reserved high nibble

admission_evidence.selects_because: purpose=principal_control with neither executed_by nor authorization_ref
admission_evidence.verification_method_source: the registration-time active update key of this unit's typed principal_registration_anchor, projected as its did:key controller proof method
admission_evidence.note: The complete wire Event is the hashed preimage plus exactly event_id and proofs, so the bytes that are hashed and the bytes that are admitted are one construction. registration_anchor is the only admission variant whose proof verification method is resolved from the anchor rather than from the current DID resolution of the actor.

registration_anchor.note: initial_resolution.did, version_id and method_history_head are the values that anchor's own terminal entry derives, and the producer proof is made by that entry's parameters.updateKeys[0]. A create Event keeping a device DID URL here cannot be the registration_anchor branch, because the branch's verifier reads the method from the anchor and requires equality.

cases.name: human_pcr_genesis_on_a_second_station_derives_a_distinct_realm_id
cases.note: A second legal genesis for the same human DID that differs from step 1 only in the account Station and the generation-0 governance Station. It proves the distinct-Realm claim by recomputation instead of assertion: one DID on two Stations is two independent, non-migratable PCRs (models/realm-and-space.md section 2.5).

founding_material.note: The genesis payload embeds this exact descriptor and the second Event carries this exact authorize payload, so the two fixtures are one construction input and not two copies that can drift apart.

cases.name: human_founding_device_authorize_binds_the_derived_realm
cases.note: Step 2 of the same atomic ordered unit [ak.realm.create, ak.device.authorize]. Its envelope realm_id and scope_ref carry the Realm derived in step 1, and its payload is the proof-free founding authorize payload whose canonical digest the step 1 descriptor already commits to. The dependency is one-way: step 1 commits to the payload digest, never to this Event id.

founding_material.note: The genesis payload embeds this exact descriptor and the second Event carries this exact authorize payload, so the two fixtures are one construction input and not two copies that can drift apart.

cases.name: same_account_second_genesis_rejected_by_station_account_uniqueness
cases.note: Account-dimension uniqueness is a state judgement, not a byte judgement. Under event-derived ids a second genesis produces a different realm_id, so no id-collision rejection can fire and nothing about this case follows from the digests or the retype equality above.

state_input.station_accounts_record: already holds an accepted principal_control Realm for this AccountId

cases.name: agent_provision_forward_declaration_is_constructible
cases.note: Constructibility proof for the encoding.md §3.1 class C exemption, step 1: the controller freezes the Agent PCR genesis envelope and derives its realm id before anything is submitted. Nothing in this preimage names the provision Event.

cases.name: agent_provision_declares_the_frozen_genesis_realm_id
cases.note: Constructibility proof step 2: the provision payload carries the realm id derived in step 1 and still hashes to a well-defined event_id. The dependency is one-way, so both Events exist; the pair is submitted in two separate submissions, never one unit or batch.

cases.name: agent_provision_and_genesis_in_one_batch_rejected
cases.mutation: submit the ak.agent.provision and its declared agent_control ak.realm.create as one atomic unit or one ordered submit batch
cases.note: The named exemption covers a later separate submission only. Inside one unit the genesis is a not-yet-formed sibling, which is the class B shape encoding.md §3.1 forbids unconditionally.

cases.name: genesis_without_accepted_provision_declaration_rejected
cases.mutation: submit the agent_control ak.realm.create while no accepted ak.agent.provision in the controller PCR declares retype(its event_id)

cases.name: two_provisions_declaring_one_realm_id_rejected
cases.mutation: submit a second ak.agent.provision whose payload.principal_control_realm_id equals an already claimed value

cases.name: suite_code_mismatch_rejected
cases.mutation: replace 0x01 with active 0x02 while retaining sha256 digest

cases.name: nonzero_event_reserved_nibble_rejected
cases.mutation: replace header 0x01 with 0x11 while retaining the same SHA-256 digest

cases.name: same_event_id_different_canonical_bytes_is_hash_collision
cases.assumption: two distinct canonical preimages hash to the same complete 256-bit digest under suite 0x01

cases.name: organization_governed_pcr_genesis_derives_a_distinct_realm
cases.note: The same human principal, the same governance Station and the same genesis object, created under explicit organization authority instead of by the principal itself. The executor pair enters canonical Event bytes, so the two branches can never derive the same Realm: the branch choice is part of the identity and not metadata beside it.

admission_evidence.selects_because: purpose=principal_control with both executed_by and authorization_ref
admission_evidence.verification_method_source: the executor's own device key, never the subject principal's
admission_evidence.note: The proof verification method resolves to executed_by and not to actor_id: the executor signs the wire write while the subject principal stays the principal of record. A self-principal verification method here would make the delegated branch indistinguishable from registration_anchor at the proof layer even though the selector already separated them.

executor_signing_material.note: Two Ed25519 keys are published conformance material, so the organization executor device key is the same published key as the founding device key. The reuse is a property of published test material and carries no protocol claim: the two signers are separated by verification_method, which resolves under the executor's own DID and not under the registration anchor.

cases.name: human_pcr_admission_selection_is_exclusive_over_the_executor_pair
cases.note: The two human PCR branches are split on the presence of the executor pair, so the split is only fail-closed if every pair combination selects exactly one variant. Absence is evaluated member by member, which is why a member that is present with a null value still counts as present.

samples.name: both_members_present_as_null
samples.note: Both members are present, so the delegated variant is selected and the null values are rejected by the closed envelope schema rather than by the selector. Routing and member validity are two gates, and routing MUST NOT be the one that notices a null.

non_overlap_rule.why: selected_branches() builds each guard as predicate_i AND NOT(any other predicate), so any two guards are disjoint by construction and a test that intersects two guards is a tautology. Overlap is only observable on the unguarded predicates.

derived_relations.why: The human genesis Event id is the suite-tagged digest of its own canonical bytes.
realm_id is the retype of that Event token, byte for byte.
The rejected token must be the accepted one with only the reserved nibble changed.
The declared human DID is the one inside the hashed bytes, not a label beside them.
Same for the account Station the genesis is attributed to.
Same for the generation-0 governance Station.
The genesis payload embeds the founding descriptor itself, not a digest of it.
project(initial_resolution.did) is recomputed with the method adapter registry and MUST land in the declared projection (key-management.md).
The projection MUST be the principal the Event is attributed to; the next relation reads that principal out of the hashed bytes.
The projected principal must also be the principal the hashed bytes attribute to.
The descriptor commits to the canonical digest of the proof-free authorize payload.
The founding device possession proof must actually verify under the descriptor key.
The second legal genesis is recomputed, not asserted.
Its realm_id is the retype of its own Event token.
The second genesis carries the same human DID as step 1.
The founding device authorize Event id is recomputed from its own canonical bytes.
Its envelope scope is the Realm derived by step 1.
So is its envelope realm_id.
Its payload is the exact proof-free authorize payload the descriptor commits to.
The collaboration Realm genesis in this fixture is derived the same way.
And its realm_id is the retype of that token.
Ordinary object retype: a Strand id is its create Event token.
Agent PCR genesis, step 1 of the two-step forward declaration.
Its realm_id is the retype of that frozen Event token.
Step 2 hashes the very Realm token step 1 derived; the declaration is not a second value.
And the value step 2 declares beside its bytes is that same Realm.

The registration_anchor branch resolves the producer key from the anchor's active update key, so the create Event's proof is verified under updateKeys[0] itself. A create Event signed by the founding device cannot pass this row.
The organization-delegated branch resolves the producer key under the executor's own DID, so its proof verifies under the executor device key and not under the anchor.
The binding object commits to the recomputed event_digest, so a proof made over some other digest cannot be reused here.
Same for the organization-delegated branch.
The wire proof and the binding object MUST name one verification method; the branch selection is read off this value.
Same for the organization-delegated branch.
The create Event's initial_resolution version_id is the anchor's derived versionId, not a caller-chosen label.
And its method_history_head is the digest of that anchor's terminal entry.
The Realm the control proof signs is the Realm this Event derives, so the transcript cannot be re-pointed at another genesis.
And the payload digest it signs is over this Event's own create payload.
